TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Japan has updated its national certification system to allow “Taiwan” to appear on professional certifications, Nikkei reported.
The change follows a policy shift last year that allowed people to enter Taiwan in Japan’s family registers. Taiwanese applicants had previously been listed as from “China” on their certifications. The revised fields can now accommodate both countries and regions.
More than 70,000 Taiwanese were living in Japan as of December, according to Japan’s Immigration Services Agency. The changes cover 322 national certifications, including those for physicians and nurses.
A Taiwanese doctor practicing in Japan told Liberty Times that he felt “relieved” to be allowed to list Taiwan on his certification. He said patients had asked why his license indicated he was from China when he told them he was Taiwanese.
Lee I-yang (李逸洋), Taiwan’s representative to Japan, thanked the Japanese legislators who had pushed for the change and described it as a major step toward protecting the rights of Taiwanese in Japan.
Keiji Furuya, a member of Japan’s House of Representatives, called the policy shift an important step in Taiwan-Japan relations. He said lawmakers would continue working toward allowing all Taiwanese residents to list “Taiwan” on their national certifications.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) faces opposition to his proposal to relocate Songshan Airport and redevelop the site as an AI park, with a recent poll showing more residents oppose the plan than support it.
A TVBS poll released Saturday found that 41% of Taipei residents opposed the proposal, compared with 31% who supported it, while 28% expressed no opinion. The survey interviewed 1,131 Taipei adults from Monday to Thursday and had a reported margin of error of plus or minus 2.9%, per TVBS.
At the opening of the Lihu Childcare Center on Monday, Chiang said he was willing to listen to views from all sectors and work with the central government to resolve difficulties associated with relocating the airport, per CNA.
Chiang said Terminal 3 at Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport, scheduled to open in 2027, and its third runway, planned for 2033, could help accommodate flights currently handled by Songshan Airport. He said the period between 2027 and 2033 could be used to review the necessary arrangements and prepare for future industrial development.
The proposal has drawn scrutiny from the central government. Cabinet Secretary-General Chang Tun-han (張惇涵) said relocating Songshan Airport could not be decided by a few people looking at PowerPoint presentations, underscoring the need for a more detailed review.
Chiang responded that the Taipei City Government had informed the central government in 2023 that relocating the airport would benefit the city’s long-term development. He added that the city began coordinating with the Ministry of National Defense in 2024 over the recovery of land at Songnan Military Camp to develop an AI industrial cluster.
The mayor has proposed transforming about 300 hectares of airport land and surrounding areas into an AI park incorporating technology businesses, residential communities, and green space.
Transportation is a point of contention. Chiang said Sunday that business travelers could reach Taipei from Taoyuan Airport in about 36 minutes using the airport MRT or elevated highways, per CNA.
DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen (沈伯洋) said the proposal did not yet provide a complete alternative to Songshan Airport. Opposition has also come from outside politics. Pegatron Chair Tung Tzu-hsien (童子賢) said relocating the airport was inadvisable, arguing that a capital should retain a regional air transport hub, per UDN.

India: End the crackdown on peaceful protests and release arbitrarily detained protesters
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:48:34 UTC
18:48:34 KST

The brutal crackdown on peaceful protesters in New Delhi over the last weekend is alarming with mass detention, unlawful use of force, the targeting of journalists, human rights defenders including lawyers, and internet shutdowns, said rights groups in a statement.
Amnesty International, CIVICUS, Front Line Defenders and South Asians for Human Rights call on the Indian authorities to release everyone arbitrarily detained for the exercise of their right to freedom of peaceful assembly and ensure accountability for abuses by security forces.
On 10 October 2026, protests were called by the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and backed by student groups calling for the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner of India, following reports that the nationwide Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls by the election commission removed around 130 million names from voter lists.
Since the call for protests, authorities used Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) to ban gatherings of more than five people. Ahead of the 10 October protest, more than 50,000 police and security personnel were reportedly deployed, some drawn from other states. Trains and buses to New Delhi were cancelled or suspended, metro train stations were closed, and the city’s borders were sealed to large vehicles. Anti-riot vehicles with tear gas launchers were stationed near protest sites.
At least 10,000 people were reportedly detained for violating prohibitory orders across India before the march, many while travelling to Delhi. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and other leaders were detained for violating prohibitory orders on 10 October after landing at Delhi airport and were held overnight. Thousands of protesters were arbitrarily detained by the police in New Delhi including journalists who were covering the protests. Others detained included student leader Neha Bora, activist Yogendra Yadav, senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee and economist Jean Drèze.
Police moved to break up the demonstrations before they could begin, intercepting demonstrators on their way to Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in central Delhi. Some were dragged away before being bundled into police vehicles and taken to temporary detention centres. Some police personnel had no visible name tags.
Arbitrary detentions continued on 11 October and there were reports of physical attacks by police on protesters in detention. Many women protesters and journalists accused security personnel of sexual harassment while detaining them during the protests.
Right-wing vigilante groups were also seen threatening and assaulting protesters and journalists. Some of them harassed Muslim women journalists while they were covering the protests.
Nearly 40 journalists were detained over the two days. Some of them were physically assaulted, intimidated, and had their camera and mobile phones seized or destroyed despite showing their press identity cards.
A group of lawyers who carried out a rally near the Supreme Court in support of protesters also faced unlawful force by police and some were detained briefly.
Instagram accounts of the news outlets Molitics and Journo Mirror have been blocked in India during its coverage of the protests citing Information Technology Rules.
On 10 October authorities also ordered a 24-hour mobile internet shutdown in central Delhi. Mobile internet was also reportedly blocked at eight stadiums used as detention centres, cutting detainees off from their lawyers and families. Reports also suggest that the shutdown was taking place beyond areas of protests and detention.
On 13 October, the Delhi Police de-notified the Jantar Mantar area in central Delhi as a protest spot and provided alternative venues further away. CJP leaders continued their protest and were arrested near Jantar Mantar. On 14 October Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka from CJP were ordered by a court to be detained in judicial custody for five-days for ‘trespassing’ in Jantar Mantar.
The right to protest is protected in India’s constitution. Demonstrations should not depend on obtaining prior permission from the police. At most, organizers may be expected to notify the authorities of their plans.
The crackdown follows the July 2026 CJP protests where human rights groups documented unlawful use of force against those protests, including pellet-firing shotguns, tear gas and no officer in Delhi Police has been held accountable.
We call on the Indian authorities to:
- Immediately and unconditionally release all those detained solely for exercising their right to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly and drop all charges against protesters, journalists and lawyers who have been arbitrarily detained
- Undertake an independent investigation of violations committed by security forces against protesters, activists and journalists including arbitrary detention, unnecessary and excessive force, ill-treatment and sexual harassment and bring those responsible to account
- Instruct all police and security personnel to respect journalists’ right to report, return seized or damaged equipment, and stop coercing journalists to delete footage or hand over personal data
- End arbitrary internet shutdowns and the blocking of accounts that cover or support protests
- Ensure that all uniformed law enforcement officials conducting policing of demonstrations must wear identity badges in visible places
- Investigate and prosecute violence by non-state actors against protesters and journalists
- Ensure that security forces follow the UN Basic Principles on the Use of Force and Firearms by Law Enforcement Officials while responding to peaceful protests
- Ensure peaceful protesters are able to demand accountability from those in power without facing intimidation, arbitrary detention, or sweeping restrictions on their freedoms.
Signed,
Amnesty International
CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
Front Line Defenders
South Asians for Human Rights (SAHR)

The International Food Exhibition Kicks Off in Paris
Italy
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:45:59 CEST
18:45:59 KST

The 2026 edition of SIAL Paris was inaugurated yesterday in Paris at the Paris Nord Villepinte exhibition center, the International Food Exhibition, in the presence of Annie Genevard, French Minister of Agriculture, Agri-Food, and Food Sovereignty, and representatives from the Italian Embassy in France. The event, scheduled to run through October 21, sees Italy once again take the lead in terms of exhibition space, with a total of approximately 700 companies participating in the fair. As part of the Italian delegation, ICE Agenzia is organizing a collective exhibition featuring 218 companies spread across Halls 1, 5B, and 7, covering a total area of approximately 3,000 m². The Italian presence offers companies an important opportunity to showcase their products of excellence to international operators and develop new business relationships with buyers, importers, and distributors.
                                    
The French market plays a leading role for the Italian agri-food sector. In fact, France is the sector’s second-largest export destination, after Germany. In 2025—the year in which Italian agri-food exports exceeded 72 billion euros worldwide—French imports of agri-food products from Italy reached 6.84 billion euros, marking a 4.78% increase compared to 2024. This positive trend continued in the first half of 2026: the value of French imports from Italy stood at 3.35 billion euros, up 2.3% compared to the same period the previous year.
                                    
The breakdown of this trade highlights the diversity of Italian production. In the first six months of 2026, French imports of Italian cheeses reached 563.7 million euros (+1.8%), those of pasta 254.7 million (+0.4%), and those of hams and cured meats 107.4 million (+5%). At SIAL, the member companies of the collective will showcase this diversity of supply chains: Hall 1 will feature gourmet specialties, Hall 5B will showcase confectionery products, and Hall 7 will highlight dairy products. For industry professionals, this will be an opportunity to meet directly with companies from different regions, all united by a focus on quality, product origin, and innovation. Participation in SIAL Paris 2026 confirms the trade show’s strategic role as an international hub for promoting the Italian agri-food sector. In France, Italy’s second-largest export market, exports reached 6.7 billion euros, up more than 5% from the previous year. Against the backdrop of slowing growth in 2026, SIAL represents a crucial opportunity to consolidate the results achieved and open up new opportunities in international markets. The Italian pavilion was inaugurated today in the presence of ICE Agency President Matteo Zoppas, who, at the conclusion of the ceremony, met with representatives from the Italian regions in attendance, the companies participating in the collective exhibition, and the main industry associations. Among the institutional guests who graced the opening ceremony were Nicola Caputo, Special Envoy of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Antonio Tajani, responsible for exports and the internationalization of the agri-food sector; and Fabio Cannavaro, Ambassador of Serie A, whose presence helped strengthen the link between the excellence of “Made in Italy,” the international promotion of Italy’s image, and the great ambassadors of Italian sports around the world.
                                    
During the event, the Italian pavilion will today welcome Luigi D’Eramo, Undersecretary of State at the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty, and Forests (MASAF), who is in Paris for the Ministerial Conference on Agriculture. The visit will provide an important opportunity to engage with Italian companies participating in SIAL and to highlight the quality and competitiveness of the national agri-food sector in international markets.

Indonesia fires ‘have burned nearly 2 mln hectares’
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:45:55 UTC
18:45:55 KST

Members of the all-women The Power of Mama (TPoM) volunteer firefighting team spray water onto smouldering peatland in Mensubuk Lama, Tanjungpura Village, Ketapang Regency, West Kalimantan on September 26, 2026. (AFP File Photo)
Fires in Indonesia burned through over 1.9 million hectares between January and the end of September this year, a monitor analyzing satellite imagery said on Oct. 19.
The figure, an area nearly 12 times larger than London, is a conservative estimate in part because haze has complicated satellite verification, said David Gaveau, founder of deforestation monitoring site Nusantara Atlas.
Indonesia’s government has not provided official figures for areas burned since announcing 202,000 hectares had been razed by the end of July.
Gaveau said the true scale of the burning was likely to be even higher than the 1,916,588 hectares his organization has detected so far.
“Our burned-area estimates are conservative for two reasons. First, we exclude individual burn scars smaller than 6.25 hectares. Second, we prioritize avoiding false detections,” he said.
This year, the calculation has also been impacted by heavy haze, which has obscured satellite images at times.
“The total reported burned area therefore underestimates the true area burned,” he said.
Even so, Nusantara Atlas data shows the area burned by the end of September this year was 38 percent higher than the same point in 2019.
The satellites the monitor uses were not available during severe fires in 2015, so comparable data is not available.

Swiss security firm accused of thousands of labour law breaches
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:44:24 UTC
18:44:24 KST

Swiss security firm accused of thousands of labour law breaches
Securitas, a Swiss company operating in the security services market, is alleged to have forced employees to work many excessively long shifts for years.
Some experts have told the Swiss public broadcaster SRF that the group’s practices constitute systematic breaches of labour law.
According to an analysis of internal data carried out by SRF Investigativ, SRF’s investigative journalism unit, there were reportedly around 20,000 breaches of the Labour Act between 2023 and 2025.
Around 900 employees are said to have been affected. The main issues are reported to have been excessively long shifts and insufficient rest periods. Staff concerned are said to have been employed in prisons, hospitals and asylum seeker centres.
All of this “is a sign of systematic practice”, Denis G. Humbert, a lawyer specialising in labour law, told SRF, calling for the authorities to intervene. “It is not permissible, it is unacceptable. This constitutes the exploitation of staff and is not allowed.”
Kurt Pärli, a professor of law at the University of Basel, echoed this view. Wat has come to light “cannot be explained away as a simple planning error. The problem with this situation goes far beyond that”.
Securitas has issued a written statement admitting that, in some cases, the practices adopted did not comply with the principles of labour law or the company’s values.
Measures taken in recent years have led to a reduction in problematic cases. The company disputes the total figure of 20,000 breaches.
While not ruling out the possibility of errors, the company said that there has been no general and systematic breach of the Labour Act.

Police investigate Grolsch beer tasting contamination
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:41:35 UTC
18:41:35 KST

Police investigate Grolsch beer tasting contamination
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
Eleven people fell ill on Saturday afternoon after tasting water during a tour of the Grolsch brewery in Enschede. The water may have been contaminated with caustic soda, according to local broadcaster RTV Oost.
The group of nine visitors and two guides had been given shot glasses of the spring water used to brew the beer, a tasting that has been part of the tour for years.
One of the victims told RTV Oost that several people noticed a strange, sour taste and a burning feeling in their stomach after drinking it. Members of the group became nauseous and vomited, and the broadcaster said they may have suffered internal burns to the throat, oesophagus and stomach.
Several ambulances went to the brewery, and a German trauma team was called out but turned out not to be needed. All 11 were out of hospital on Sunday, and one spent the night in hospital, Grolsch told public broadcaster NOS.
Police have started a forensic investigation, and the labour inspectorate is also investigating. A police spokesperson told NOS it could have been an accident, “or something else could be going on”.
Grolsch said the tap the group drank from is separate from the rest of the production process, and that the quality and safety of its beer “are not and have not been at risk”. The company said it would not comment on possible causes while the investigation is ongoing.

Shivraj Singh Chouhan hits back at Rahul Gandhi over ‘expiry date’ remark on BJP

AI recordings of doctor-patient conversations the new norm for Estonian hospitals
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:41:00 UTC
18:41:00 KST

AI recordings of doctor-patient conversations the new norm for Estonian hospitals
Artificial intelligence systems that record conversations between patients and doctors, produce written summaries and help physicians make diagnoses and recommend next steps are already a reality in a number of hospitals.
Confido CEO Edvard Garder told ERR that the company began testing AI solutions last year, making it one of the first in Estonia to do so.
"The solution is now in use in several departments and we plan to roll it out across the entire organization. Patients have responded positively to the solution because doctors have more time to spend with them," Garder said.
Narva Hospital is currently seeking Estonian-language speech recognition and transcription software through a public procurement process. The software would convert conversations between doctors or nurses and patients into electronic text that can be processed, automatically translated, played back and stored.
Narva Hospital also wants the AI assistant to suggest medical codes and support doctors in making decisions. However, the procurement requirements emphasize that doctors must remain the decision-makers in all processes. AI-generated content that has not been reviewed and approved by a healthcare professional must not be entered into patients' medical records.
Tartu University Hospital began testing AI in its emergency department in mid-October and plans to continue the trial for three months. If the technology proves useful, the hospital will extend the trial period to obtain definitive confirmation of the application's benefits.
"The aim of using the EMO24 application is to reduce the time doctors and nurses spend on documentation. It also helps eliminate duplication where patients have to describe their condition to different staff members multiple times," said Aime Keis, head of the hospital's emergency department.
Heba Clinic also uses AI to compile patients' medical histories before appointments, document conversations during visits and subsequently prepare summaries and explanations for patients.
Heba Clinic CEO Ain Aaviksoo noted in an opinion article (in Estonian — ed.) published by ERR last week that AI cannot make decisions on behalf of doctors but should support solutions that help people manage their own health and enable doctors to assist them in doing so.
Every hospital looking for its own AI assistant
The Ministry of Social Affairs has not conducted a comprehensive assessment of the current use of artificial intelligence solutions across all hospitals, said Nele Labi, the ministry's deputy secretary general for innovation. However, the ministry is aware of several initiatives.
"We see that private hospitals have generally made the fastest progress in testing new solutions," Labi added.
According to Labi, there is no unified nationwide system to help hospitals streamline their work using AI and hospitals are largely seeking solutions independently based on their own needs.
"At the national level, however, two major AI-based solutions are currently under development: a transcription tool for family medicine and a transcription tool for the electronic ambulance system. The state has several other AI projects, but these two are expected to have the greatest impact on healthcare professionals' administrative workload in the near future," the deputy secretary general said.
Confido's CEO noted that healthcare professionals welcome the opportunities offered by AI and that skepticism is relatively rare. According to Garder, there is no significant difference between medical specialties in terms of the potential benefits as automated transcription tools and clinical decision support systems can reduce the documentation burden in virtually every field.
"This gives doctors more time for direct interaction with patients and also means that discharge summaries and other medical reports reach the national health portal more quickly," he said.
However, adopting AI does not mean immediate cost savings for hospitals, as initial investments are required. Garder nevertheless believes the technology will help reduce workloads and burnout among doctors and nurses, although the financial benefits of improved employee well-being cannot always be measured precisely.
The Ministry of Social Affairs also confirmed that projects in other European countries have clearly demonstrated the positive impact of such solutions in reducing administrative workloads.
"Estonia's approach is to seamlessly integrate general-purpose tools such as speech recognition and transcription into our hospitals' workflows so that medical professionals can spend their time on patients rather than paperwork," the deputy secretary general said.
Patients must be notified of AI involvement
A separate question is how to ensure that information exchanged between patients and doctors remains confidential and does not fall into the wrong hands.
According to Garder, Confido considers the solutions it currently uses to be secure and continues to do everything possible to mitigate potential risks. Nevertheless, Confido patients have the option to decline the use of AI during their appointments.
Tartu University Hospital also said participation in its AI pilot project is voluntary. If an emergency department patient does not wish to use the application, information gathering, diagnosis and treatment will proceed as before.
The Ministry of Social Affairs' deputy secretary general confirmed that strict data protection rules apply to the processing of such information and that patients must be informed about recordings and their purpose.
"However, because the technology is developing very rapidly, we need greater legal clarity and must ensure that patients understand how it is used and that the process is transparent. Working groups have already been established at the ministry to address this issue," Labi said.
Confido's CEO believes the state should develop a standard for security criteria. However, Garder does not consider it necessary for the state to develop a single AI solution for all healthcare institutions.
"Especially since tying all healthcare providers to a single system would create a monopoly and stifle innovation. Moreover, I'm not sure that would be the most efficient use of public funds," Garder said.
Instead, he believes the state should focus on ensuring that all data in the national health portal can be processed by AI, which would in turn speed up preparations for medical appointments.
"At present, the state is clearly moving far too slowly in adopting AI," the Confido CEO said.
--
Editor: Marcus Turovski

Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva reportedly returns to coach Eteri Tutberidze
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva reportedly returns to coach Eteri Tutberidze
Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva has resumed training with Eteri Tutberidze’s team, a source told the Russian state news agency TASS. There had been no official statement on the matter as of the time of publication.
Valieva, 20, trained under Tutberidze for years, setting world records in the short program, the free skate, and the combined score of both programs. She was considered one of the top contenders for medals heading into the 2022 Winter Olympics. During the Games, one of Valieva’s doping tests came back positive. She won gold in the team event but left the individual competition without a medal.
In 2024, Valieva was still disqualified for four years over doping, and the results of Russian figure skaters’ performances in the team event were revised. In 2025, Valieva and Tutberidze ended their partnership, and Svetlana Sokolovskaya became her coach.
In January 2026, Valieva resumed her career after her disqualification ended (calculated from the date the violation was recorded) and even obtained neutral athlete status. But in September, the International Skating Union (ISU) revoked that status.

S. Korean president reaffirms commitment to early recovery of wartime operational control from U.S.
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
17:38:53 CST
18:38:53 KST

SEOUL, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Monday reaffirmed his firm commitment to the early recovery of South Korea's wartime operational control (OPCON) from the United States.
Lee said during a press conference that Seoul must and definitely can retrieve it ahead of schedule, saying that the term "transfer" regarding OPCON, which had been used previously, should be changed to terms such as recovery or retrieval.
Lee underscored that military sovereignty is one of the most critical core components of national sovereignty, saying OPCON must be recovered swiftly to meet the minimum requirements of a sovereign state.
Expressing his firm confidence in the independent defense capabilities of the South Korean military, Lee said South Korea should and is fully capable of handling its own defense.
In the early 1950s, South Korea handed over command of its military to the U.S.-led "United Nations Command." In 1978, it was then transferred to the South Korea-U.S. Combined Forces Command, which is headed by a U.S. military officer. South Korea retook peacetime operational control of its forces in 1994, but has not yet regained wartime operational control. ■

BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China firmly opposes and strongly condemns Japan's negative moves concerning the Yasukuni Shrine, and has lodged stern representations and strong protests with the Japanese side, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said Monday.
Spokesperson Mao Ning made the remarks at a daily media briefing in Beijing after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent a ritual offering and monetary donation to the Yasukuni Shrine on Oct. 17 and 19, while multiple Japanese government officials, senior officials of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and parliamentarians paid visits to the site recently.

Such acts lay bare their deep-rooted erroneous perceptions on historical issues, as well as their sinister attempt to exonerate war criminals, reverse the verdict on aggression and pave the way for remilitarization," Mao said.
Noting this year marks 80 years of the opening of the Tokyo Trials, the spokesperson once again solemnly urged Japan to face up to history, reflect on its crimes, stop retrogressive acts on historical issues, and win trust from its Asian neighbors and the international community with concrete actions. ■

Powerlifter Cui Zhe sets personal best to win China's 1st gold at Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
17:38:51 CST
18:38:51 KST

NAGOYA, Japan, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- Powerlifter Cui Zhe led from her opening attempt to win the women's 41kg title at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games on Monday, delivering China's first gold medal of the Games.
"This is my fifth Asian Para Games, and I'm so happy to win the first gold for China today," Cui said. "I want to thank my country, our coaching team and everyone back home who has supported me."
Cui also won China's first gold medal at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, where she claimed the women's 41kg title with a decisive final lift. Eight years later and less than two months shy of her 40th birthday, she opened Monday's competition with a confident 110kg lift, immediately putting herself 10kg ahead of nearest rival Tursynay Kabyl of Kazakhstan.
Cui extended her lead with a 115kg second lift. When Kabyl, the penultimate lifter, selected 104kg for her third attempt, Cui's gold was secured. The champion was not finished, however. She called for 120kg on her final attempt and completed the lift cleanly, surpassing the personal best of 119kg she set at the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games. After the lift was declared good, Cui turned to the crowd, waved and smiled broadly.
"I focused on staying calm because I had never lifted that weight in competition. I just wanted to get every detail right," she said.
Cui's victory extended a remarkable streak, as she has competed at all five editions of the Asian Para Games and won gold at each one. A Paralympic veteran since Beijing 2008, she finally claimed Paralympic gold in Paris in 2024.
Looking ahead, Cui sees Nagoya as part of her build-up to Los Angeles 2028. "I view this as a test on the road to the 2028 Paralympics. I hope I can lift even better there," she said.
Earlier on Monday, China's Chen Liuxun secured the delegation's first medal of the Games, taking bronze in the men's 49kg para powerlifting with a best lift of 161kg. ■

BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's investment in innovation-driven sectors held up well in the first three quarters of 2026, even as overall fixed-asset investment continued to contract, official data showed on Monday.

While overall growth has slowed, investment is playing an increasingly important role in optimizing supply and driving innovation, Mao Shengyong, deputy head of the NBS, told a press conference on Monday.
Analysts said the current pullback in overall investment reflects a transition from a traditional investment model to a new one.
"Investment is undergoing a profound shift in emphasis from traditional sectors to emerging ones, and from scale expansion to efficiency improvement," said Liu Yuanchun, president of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics.
China's effective investment space remains vast over the medium and long term, Liu said, noting that artificial intelligence (AI) and new infrastructure will serve as key engines for the next round of effective investment.
The expansion of AI applications is spurring sustained investment across industrial chains.
NBS data revealed that in the first three quarters of 2026, investment in electronic circuit manufacturing surged 58.7 percent year on year, and integrated circuit manufacturing investment rose 14.2 percent. Meanwhile, companies are accelerating their shift toward intelligent operations, driving a 9.7 percent increase in investment in equipment and tools purchases.
In terms of new infrastructure, China's "six networks" initiative, covering water, power, computing, communications, urban underground pipelines and logistics networks, represents a major investment opportunity. It is estimated that investment in these six networks and related areas will exceed 7 trillion yuan in 2026.
Investment will increasingly serve the development of new quality productive forces and the building of a modern industrial system, with the ultimate results felt in expanded employment, rising incomes and improved living standards, Liu said. ■

BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's industrial sector continued to gain momentum in the first three quarters of 2026, with high-tech and equipment manufacturing expanding rapidly, official data showed Monday.
The country's value-added industrial output increased by 5.3 percent year on year in the first nine months of 2026, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS).
In September, value-added industrial output rose 5.5 percent year on year, accelerating by 0.3 percentage points from August, the data showed.
Despite a complex environment, China's industrial sector maintained steady growth and made further progress in the first three quarters, Mao Shengyong, deputy head of the NBS, said at a press conference.
NBS data showed value-added output of equipment manufacturing grew 10.2 percent year on year in the first three quarters, while high-tech manufacturing rose 14.3 percent. Both outpaced overall industrial growth by 4.9 and 9 percentage points, respectively.
Equipment and high-tech manufacturing accounted for 37.6 percent and 18.3 percent of value-added industrial output during the period, respectively, Mao said, describing them as key drivers of industrial transformation and high-quality development.
Industrial output is used to measure the activity of large enterprises each with an annual main business revenue of at least 20 million yuan (about 2.98 million U.S. dollars).
At the product level, output of industrial robots jumped 29.1 percent year on year, while 3D printing equipment and lithium-ion batteries saw increases of 62.5 percent and 39.5 percent, respectively.
New growth drivers, represented by high-end manufacturing, the digital and intelligent economy, and modern services, contributed more than 40 percent to China's economic growth in the first nine months, Mao said, citing preliminary estimates.
"The baton of economic growth is being passed increasingly to new growth drivers," he said.
The figures reflect China's broader push to upgrade its industrial structure and cultivate new growth drivers. The country's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) underscores the development of a modernized industrial system with advanced manufacturing as its backbone.
Earlier this month, China issued guidelines to accelerate the development of new quality productive forces. The measures include advancing scientific and technological innovation, deepening the integration of sci-tech and industrial innovation, and innovating development approaches.
Overall, China's economy remained generally stable in the first three quarters, with new growth drivers gaining strength and the economic structure continuing to improve, Mao said. ■

BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's job market remained generally stable in the first three quarters of 2026, with the surveyed urban unemployment rate declining in September, official data showed on Monday.
The average surveyed urban unemployment rate stood at 5.2 percent in the first nine months of the year, unchanged from the same period of 2025, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS).
In September alone, the surveyed urban unemployment rate came in at 5.2 percent, down 0.1 percentage points from the previous month.
The surveyed unemployment rate among workers with local household registration was 5.2 percent, while that among workers with non-local household registration stood at 5.1 percent. The rate for migrant workers with rural household registration was 5.0 percent.
The services sector remained a main driver of employment, accounting for 49.4 percent of the country's total workforce. Employment increased in sectors including transportation, accommodation and catering, as well as culture, sports and entertainment, according to Mao Shengyong, deputy head of the NBS.
Since the beginning of the year, China has introduced a series of policies to boost employment, with a target to keep the surveyed urban unemployment rate around 5.5 percent in 2026 and create more than 12 million new urban jobs during the year.
China released a five-year plan on human resources and social security development in July. Among other targets for the 2026-2030 period, the plan aims to help 25 million unemployed urban workers find new jobs and provide employment assistance to 6.5 million people having difficulty finding work.
The country is also stepping up efforts to adapt its labor market to rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI), seeking to harness technological innovation to create jobs while addressing its impact on employment.
A five-year plan on implementing the employment-first strategy identified promoting employment amid AI advances as a key task, calling for creating jobs through AI applications and tapping the potential in traditional sectors. ■

The new case comes after the country announced four new Ebola cases on Saturday, including a close male relative of the country's first patient and three health workers who attended to him while he was in hospital.
Amoth further allayed fears of community transmission, saying there was a low possibility that the quarantined persons transmitted the disease at community level.
According to the Ministry of Health, authorities have actively traced contacts and placed individuals exposed to confirmed cases under quarantine.
As of Oct. 17, health officials had identified 130 contacts of the first patient and traced 128 of them, the Ministry of Health said. Contact tracing for the cases confirmed since then is continuing.
Kenya confirmed its first Ebola case on Oct. 6. The index patient, a Kenyan man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), arrived in Nairobi on Oct. 3.
The patient died while undergoing treatment at a Nairobi hospital and was later accorded a safe and dignified burial at a public cemetery to minimize the risk of transmission. ■

====================================================================================================

Lost Arctic sandpiper spotted in the Negev
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:33:51 UTC
18:33:51 KST

On a cool autumnal Friday in mid-October, birdwatcher Miriam Al-Sirhan spotted an anomalous bird on the shores of an artificial lake in the Negev. It turned out to be an extremely lost North American buff-breasted sandpiper.
This was just the second time a buff-breasted sandpiper has been spotted in Israel, which is on the other side of the planet from their usual stamping ground and migration route. Al-Sirhan saw the animal at the Pora Reservoir, an artificial lake created in the Negev by damming the seasonal Pora Stream in the 1960s.
The first sighting of a sandpiper in Israel was in 2018, in Kibbutz Ga'ash, says the Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel.
The Pora Reservoir is seasonal, filling with water in the winter rainy season, when it becomes an attraction for tourists and migratory birds, apparently including this one.
Buff-breasted sandpipers breed from May to July in the Arctic Circle, specifically northern Alaska and Canada. Come the fall, they start a 10,000-kilometer migration to South America, chiefly Argentina.
Before climate change, the sandpipers would time their northbound return to the start of the thaw, as plants start to burst through the ice and insects proliferate. However, according to the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, the Arctic Circle is warming nearly four times faster than the global average. Some areas such as the Barents Sea in winter have registered warming seven times the average rate of global warming. Local temperatures can be ten degrees and more above normal.
This is terrible for the sandpiper. Some birds are proving more adaptable to climate change, some less so. This one seems to be rigid about the timing of its migration and that is a problem for it.
"The birds most affected by global warming are the ones breeding nearest to the poles, where climate change is the most intense," explains Yoav Perlman, director of the Birdwatching Center at the Society for the Protection of Nature. "Before climate change, there was a perfect match between the sandpipers' migration timing and the start of spring. But spring is arriving earlier and earlier in the Arctic," while the bird is not.
Thus the sandpiper is losing ground in the competition over the best breeding grounds and the best bugs to eat, for instance. It's missing peak productivity in insects. To who? To other species of birds that arrive in a timely fashion; or even to earlier arrivers of their own species.
It is classified as globally vulnerable, the third-highest threat level, due to climate change and horrendous habitat destruction as well as hunting. Hunting is not a problem for it in Israel because hunting in general hasn't been a common local pastime since the advent of herbivore domestication, and also, it doesn't live here.
How did it get here from its Arctic breeding grounds? Perlman's best theory is that it's a young bird on its first migration, and her inner GPS went haywire, or she got blown off course by a storm. (We don't know it's a girl – with the buff-breasted sandpiper, sexes look alike.)
"She may have crossed the Atlantic Ocean, reached Western Europe, and from there made her way to us here in Israel. This theory is supported by the fact that about a week ago, a sandpiper was spotted for the first time in neighboring Cyprus," he adds, and it has no business being there either. Maybe it was the same one and as it doggedly continued flying south, it crossed the Mediterranean to the Negev.
How serious is it to get to the Arctic late, after spring has begun? Perlman gives the analogy of showing up after 10 to a party called for eight o'clock. The best food is gone, though some pizza crusts are scattered on the table. Bon appetit. The good wine is gone, leaving rotgut, and the best mates have been selected. The sandpiper makes do, but may have fewer chicks, or the offspring it does have may fledge and leave for its own migration in sub-optimal physiological condition. The parents can't prove optimal care.
Their migration route is imprinted but it happens that some get lost. Asked if this year's El Nino weather pattern may have created stronger storms that "captured" this poor creature, he says who knows and it could be; but birds get lost all the time.
"The sandpipers' original migration route is already extremely long. If everything goes well it's about over 10,000 kilometers each way, on average, which is a huge distance to start with. If something happens to the bird when it starts flying, or during the flight, maybe the GPS in their brain gets busted, they can get lost and just keep going in the wrong direction," he says.
Note that she isn't the first or second buff breasted sandpiper to get lost. Occasionally the odd bird is reported from the Indian subcontinent or even Australia.
Is she doomed? Maybe. Or she could have a blast in the balmy Mediterranean. "We have evidence of birds that are very lost but survive somehow and keep returning year after year – they keep migrating to the wrong place," Perlman says. "It is super-rare but there's one example of a pacific golden plover [also a North American bird] that keeps returning to the same rocks on Tel Baruch beach, now for the 10th year!"
Asked how long plovers live, he answered, some live as much as 15-20 years, though it has been pointed out to Haaretz that nobody has caught this bird year after year to analyze its DNA, so maybe it isn't the same one. Probably is, though. What are the odds. "Heaven knows where it spends the summer. Then it returns to Tel Baruch in the middle of August or in September and spends the winter in Tel Aviv, leaving in March," he adds.
Before hiring mourners to wail over the plover and sandpiper, Perlman points out that they might not be victims of evil fate but pioneers. "Migratory birds getting lost isn't a new phenomenon, it happens every year, all the time and is an important evolutionary process, shaping distribution changes and colonization among bird species," he says.
Our sandpiper might miraculously survive and keep migrating on the wrong side of the planet year after year, and push the boundaries of her species, discovering new grounds and regions, however inadvertently. "That is how species spread around the world on an evolutionary scale," he sums up. "Most pioneers don't survive, but one in 100,000 or a million does and [in this way] birds spread to new regions."
Can we do anything to help the plight of the plover and sandpiper? Yes, stop fouling the planet, stop hunting them, and work hand in hand with Nature to try to heal the damage already done, he says. Israel particularly needs to nurture its lakes, artificial and otherwise, on which migrating birds depend. "Their lives are becoming more and more challenging with habitat loss and global warming, and more and more hunting along the flyways" – again, not in Israel, but everywhere else, he adds when asked about it. But we too need to do our duty.

10 arrested after attack on European diplomats in West Bank
The police operation took place in the Benjamin region, an area in the occupied West Bank, just north and north-east of Jerusalem. According to police, there is evidence that the 10 suspects were involved in Saturday’s violence.
The group was attacked near Taybeh, a Palestinian Christian village in the West Bank, by masked Israelis. The delegation – which was visiting to show solidarity with locals during the olive harvest – included the Belgian consul-general in Jerusalem, Anick Van Calster, and representatives from France and Poland. A French mayor was attacked and a Belgian diplomatic vehicle was damaged.

The violence has truly reached new heights.”
The suspects are being questioned and are due to appear before a judge. Police also seized vehicles and other potential evidence. According to the local police commissioner, they will be treated with a “professional, equal and impartial approach”.
However, the investigation goes beyond the violence perpetrated by the settlers. A preliminary investigation suggests that the Israeli army may have failed to act on several warnings.
The first reports of threats by settlers are said to have come in at around 13.00, but no soldiers or police officers were present to prevent the attack. The army was not officially notified of the incident until around 15.00, after the attack had already ended. A separate investigation into that response is to be carried out.
According to Palestinian reports, settlers in Taybeh stole money and around 25 sheep. Elsewhere, they are said to have sprayed graffiti and attempted to set vehicles alight.

Anick Van Calster
Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu initially cast doubt on the reports, suggesting they were part of a coordinated campaign to cast Israel and the settlers in a bad light.
The Israeli government also said the delegation had not coordinated its visit with the army in advance. Belgium disputes that this is a requirement under international law. The EU and the countries concerned are demanding that the perpetrators be held to account.

The cause of Monday's suspected hazardous materials leak has not yet been established, and it remains unclear whether any dangerous substances were released.

F-35C makes first arrested landing on Ford carrier
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
10:31:39 BST
18:31:39 KST

A US Navy F-35C Lightning II has completed the first arrested landing by the type aboard a Gerald R. Ford-class aircraft carrier, with the milestone taking place aboard the future USS John F. Kennedy during aircraft compatibility testing in the Atlantic, according to the US Navy.
The landing took place on 13 October aboard Pre-Commissioning Unit John F. Kennedy, designated CVN 79, as the second carrier of the Ford class continues testing ahead of its planned delivery to the Navy.
Aircraft from Air Test and Evaluation Squadron 23, known as the “Salty Dogs”, have been operating from the carrier during the trials. Imagery released the following day shows an F-35C conducting a touch-and-go from John F. Kennedy’s flight deck as testing continued on 14 October.
The current programme is focused on Aircraft Compatibility Testing, which assesses whether the ship’s launch and recovery equipment can safely and reliably support the different aircraft expected to operate from the carrier during service. For the F-35C, that means operating with two of the defining systems introduced by the Ford class: the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System, or EMALS, and Advanced Arresting Gear.
EMALS replaces the steam catapults used aboard the preceding Nimitz-class carriers with an electrically driven system for accelerating aircraft from the flight deck. Advanced Arresting Gear performs the other half of the carrier aviation cycle, absorbing the energy of an arriving aircraft when its tailhook catches one of the arresting wires stretched across the deck.
The F-35C is the carrier variant of the Joint Strike Fighter and was developed specifically for conventional US Navy aircraft carriers. It uses larger wings than the F-35A and F-35B, strengthened landing gear and a tailhook for arrested recoveries, allowing it to operate from carriers equipped with catapults and arresting gear.
Testing continued on 14 October with touch-and-go operations from the carrier. In imagery released by the US military, an F-35C from VX-23 is seen just above John F. Kennedy’s flight deck with its landing gear extended during one of the test sorties.
The US Navy said the carrier was underway conducting Aircraft Compatibility Testing, describing the work as an assessment of the operational capabilities of the ship’s aircraft launch and recovery equipment with Navy aircraft.
John F. Kennedy is the second Gerald R. Ford-class carrier, following USS Gerald R. Ford, which entered service in 2017. The class introduces a substantially redesigned aviation system compared with the Nimitz class, including EMALS, Advanced Arresting Gear, a revised flight deck layout and increased electrical generating capacity.
The carrier displaces around 100,000 tonnes at full load and is powered by two A1B nuclear reactors. Its flight deck measures more than 330 metres in length, with the class designed to operate a large embarked air wing including F/A-18E/F Super Hornets, EA-18G Growlers, E-2D Advanced Hawkeyes, helicopters and F-35Cs.
John F. Kennedy also differs from the lead ship in several areas, including its radar fit. From CVN 79 onwards, the class uses the AN/SPY-6(V)3 Enterprise Air Surveillance Radar together with the AN/SPQ-9B surface search radar rather than the dual-band arrangement installed aboard USS Gerald R. Ford. The ship remains in its pre-commissioning phase, with delivery expected in 2027. The latest aviation trials are part of the wider test programme required before the carrier can enter service and begin the process of integrating a full air wing.
The arrested landing on 13 October marked the first time an F-35C had completed a carrier recovery aboard a Ford-class ship, followed immediately by further flight deck testing as John F. Kennedy continues preparations for operational service.

Historic town hall in Limoges set on fire during French protests
Significant parts of the 143-year-old Limoges Town Hall in France have been destroyed in an arson attack, as protests broke out across the country over the weekend.
On 17th October, Limoges Town Hall was set on fire. Videos taken by people on the ground show its slate roofs ablaze and its central bell tower collapsing.
Officials have not yet confirmed the state of the town hall and whether the rest of the building is at risk of collapse, according to the BBC.
Designed by French architect Charles-Alfred Leclerc, the neo-Renaissance Limoges Town Hall was built in 1883 and was listed as a historical monument in 1975.
View this post on Instagram
The neo-Renaissance Limoges Town Hall has been damaged in a fire
An estimated 550,000 people in France took to the streets over the weekend to protest the rising cost of living and poor school conditions.
Some demonstrations turned to violence and disorder, with hundreds of shops being looted and destroyed. Around 2,400 people have been arrested.
In addition to Limoges Town Hall, other buildings in France were set on fire in arson attacks, including a tourist office in Lyon.
The mayor of Limoges has demanded a "Notre-Dame plan" to restore the town hall. A huge fire broke out at the iconic Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris in 2019, which saw the Gothic landmark's 90-metre-high spire and parts of the roof collapse.
After five years of reconstruction work, the cathedral reopened in 2024 with restored interiors and the spire rebuilt as a replica of the 1859 version lost to the fire.

Which Grade of Titanium Is Best?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:29:21 UTC
18:29:21 KST

which grade of titanium is best depends on the application rather than a universal ranking. Grade 2 can suit projects that prioritize corrosion resistance and formability, while Grade 5 may be considered when higher strength is required.
The choice also depends on service conditions and specifications. Buyers can compare titanium grade 2 in Italy, titanium grade 2 in France, and titanium grade 2 in the UK according to project requirements.
 
This guide compares common grades and explains how to make a reliable selection before purchasing titanium.
What Makes One Titanium Grade More Suitable Than Another?
Titanium grades are not interchangeable. Commercially pure and alloyed grades provide combinations of strength, corrosion resistance, formability, and fabrication characteristics.
 
Important factors include:
·     Corrosion resistance and chemical exposure
 
·     Mechanical strength and fatigue requirements
 
·     Weight and strength-to-weight performance
 
·     Forming, machining, and welding requirements
 
·     Operating temperature and service environment
 
·     Applicable specifications and certification
 
·     Product form, dimensions, and availability
Titanium grade selection should start with the component conditions.
Is Grade 2 Always the Best Titanium Grade?
No. For this application, which grade of titanium is best should be assessed first. Grade 2 is a commercially pure titanium grade with a useful balance of corrosion resistance, moderate mechanical properties, and formability.
It can be relevant to chemical processing, marine service, and other applications where corrosion performance matters. The best titanium grade is therefore application-specific.
 
Grade 5, commonly known as Ti-6Al-4V, provides substantially higher strength for demanding structural components. However, greater strength does not automatically mean it is the right material. Fabrication, corrosion conditions, specifications, and procurement requirements may lead to another choice.
 
A practical titanium grade comparison considers the complete property profile rather than one strength value.
Common Titanium Grades at a Glance
Common Titanium Grades at a Glance
 
This table shows why the best grade of titanium depends on the component requirements.
Where Does Titanium Grade 2 Fit?
Grade 2 is often selected when corrosion resistance is important and extreme strength is not the primary design requirement. Its properties can also make fabrication practical for many components.
For procurement teams, a titanium grade comparison is one part of the evaluation. Buyers may need to verify the specification, dimensions, batch identification, test reports, certification, and traceability.
Material traceability is especially important for industrial projects. Clear documentation supports receiving inspection, quality control, and later verification of the material used in a component.
Which Grade of Titanium Is Best for Different Industries?
Industry requirements can change the suitable grade.
Aerospace and High-Performance Components
Aerospace components can emphasize low weight, mechanical performance, qualification, specifications, and traceability. Grade 5 may be considered where high strength is central, while other components may require different grades or specifications.
 
The decision should follow the engineering specification.
Oil & Gas and Process Equipment
Process equipment may face aggressive chemicals, elevated temperatures, pressure, and demanding fabrication conditions. Grade 2 can be relevant when its corrosion resistance and mechanical profile match the service environment. Grade 7 may also be considered for certain corrosive conditions.
 
Medium, concentration, temperature, pressure, and applicable standards should be reviewed before confirmation.
Marine Applications
Marine service can make corrosion resistance a major consideration. Titanium may be suitable for selected components exposed to seawater or other corrosive conditions, but the actual service environment, mechanical loads, fabrication method, and project specification still need review.
Energy and Industrial Manufacturing
Industrial projects can combine mechanical, corrosion, fabrication, and documentation requirements. The selected titanium grade should satisfy the technical requirement without unnecessary material or procurement constraints.
A Practical Titanium Grade Selection Process
Rather than starting with a grade name, engineers and buyers can follow these steps:
1. Define the operating environment: Identify corrosion exposure, temperature, pressure, and other service conditions.
2. Set mechanical requirements: Determine strength, ductility, fatigue, and weight requirements.
3. Review fabrication needs: Consider forming, machining, welding, heat treatment, and component geometry.
4. Check project specifications: Confirm whether a code, customer requirement, or approved material list limits acceptable grades.
5. Verify documentation: Review certification, testing, heat numbers, dimensions, and traceability.
6.     Compare supply options: Check product form, dimensions, lead time, and availability after technical requirements are established.
 
This process turns the question "which grade of titanium is best" into a structured procurement decision. It also helps determine which titanium grade is best for the actual service conditions.
 
Why Documentation Matters Alongside Grade Selection
A material certificate should establish material identity and conformity. Alloy360 describes its VANTAGE program as including document review, physical verification, and independent third-party inspection before shipment.
 
Its published process includes checking material certificates against applicable specifications, PMI testing, visual inspection, dimensional and quantity checks, and photographic or video documentation. Third-party verification may also involve organizations such as SGS, TÜV, or Bureau Veritas.
For demanding procurement, certified material and full traceability can reduce uncertainty by connecting material with inspection records.
 
Alloy360 states that it supplies titanium, nickel alloys, stainless steel, and alloy steels to OEMs, EPCs, and manufacturers in sectors including aerospace, oil and gas, marine, and energy. Its procurement information emphasizes traceability and engineering-focused support.
Choosing Titanium by Requirement, Not Reputation
The answer to which grade of titanium is best depends on the specific engineering requirement. Grade 2 suits applications requiring corrosion resistance and formability, while Grade 5 is considered when higher strength is needed. Grades 7, 9, and 23 may meet other technical requirements.
Before ordering, buyers should confirm the grade, dimensions, product form, certification, and specifications. This applies to sourcing titanium grade 2 in Italy, titanium grade 2 in France, or titanium grade 2 in the UK.
Have a specific titanium grade, specification, or application in mind? Share the requirement or question you are working with, then use the Alloy360 site as a reference point for reviewing the available material and documentation options before moving forward with a purchase.
Final Takeaway
Before choosing a titanium grade, ask which combination of corrosion resistance, strength, formability, specification, documentation, and availability the application requires. Grade 2 and Grade 5 serve different purposes, so the best grade of titanium may differ according to the project. Other grades can also be appropriate when a project calls for a different balance.

Rubio Vows To Keep Pushing For Ukraine Peace, Seeks Deeper US Ties In Central Asia
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:29:21 UTC
18:29:21 KST

SAMARKAND -- US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington would continue efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine, warning that the conflict risks escalating beyond the two countries as he met with Central Asian officials in Uzbekistan.
Speaking to reporters in Samarkand on October 19, Rubio defended President Donald Trump's push for negotiations with Moscow and Kyiv, acknowledged limited progress, and said Washington remained open to any opportunity to secure a settlement.
“No one's winning that war,” Rubio said. “People are dying every day. Things are being blown up every day. Things are being destroyed every day.”
Rubio's visit, which brought nearly 300 American business representatives to Uzbekistan, also highlighted Washington's efforts to expand economic ties with Central Asia, a region where China has become the leading trading partner while Russia retains longstanding security and economic links.
Meeting with the foreign ministers of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan under the C5+1 framework, Rubio said the US wanted to strengthen its presence without demanding that regional governments choose between competing powers.
Asked about reports that Russian President Vladimir Putin had proposed a meeting with Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war, Rubio said discussions about a possible meeting had taken place but that he did not believe all arrangements had been finalized.
Trump remained committed to ending the conflict, Rubio said, adding that Washington would continue testing opportunities for negotiations despite the lack of progress so far.
“This is not a criminal case,” Rubio said when asked what evidence the administration had that Putin was serious about peace talks. “This is about diplomacy, and in diplomacy, you continue to try.”
He said a deal would ultimately depend on whether both sides were willing to make concessions.
Rubio: Dangers Beyond Ukraine
Rubio also defended the administration's decision to suspend certain sanctions for 60 days, saying it was intended to give ongoing talks with Russia and Ukraine a chance to produce results.
He cited the war's mounting human and economic costs, referring to Trump's repeated claim that as many as 25,000 people are dying each month in the fighting.
Rubio warned that the conflict posed dangers beyond Ukraine and Russia, particularly for Eastern Europe. Drones disrupted by electronic warfare, failed sabotage operations, and other incidents could cause damage in neighboring countries and risk triggering a wider confrontation, he said.
The US wanted to bring the war to an end because of both its devastating consequences and the risk of escalation, Rubio added.
Asked about Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's assertion that Washington had temporarily paused some intelligence sharing with Kyiv before resuming it, Rubio said there had been no interruption.
“I don't know where he's getting these things from or why he's saying these things to the press,” Rubio said.
He also declined to comment on reports that Ukraine had not received advance warning before Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv, saying he did not know the details of that incident. He acknowledged that US officials had examined a software problem involving Ukraine's early-warning system in an earlier episode.
Rubio said Washington had not changed its diplomatic presence in Kyiv, although the safety of US diplomats and facilities remained a concern.
Asked whether relations between the Trump and Zelenskyy administrations had fundamentally broken down, Rubio said Washington's priority was to end the war.
He acknowledged that Ukraine wanted to expand its use of the Starshield satellite communications system, which is controlled by the US Department of War, to conduct attacks beyond Ukrainian territory. He declined to discuss those negotiations further.
US Seeks To Compete With China
Rubio's visit also underscored Washington's ambition to gain a stronger economic foothold in Central Asia, where China is the principal trading partner of all five countries.
Chinese companies have secured deals involving regional energy resources and minerals, while Russia remains connected to the region through pipelines, security arrangements, and labor migration. Moscow's invasion of Ukraine has encouraged Central Asian governments to diversify their international relationships.
Asked how the US intended to compete with China, Rubio said Washington was seeking a fair opportunity for American businesses rather than asking regional governments to sever existing ties.
“This is not about coming here to say stop talking to somebody else or stop working with some other country,” he said.
Rubio said the US delegation had come to identify investment and trade opportunities, with agreements worth billions of dollars expected to be announced.
Uzbekistan, he added, wanted to maintain relationships with multiple powers. “They want to be friends to everybody,” Rubio said of the Uzbek government. “They want to have a relationship with everybody.”
He described Uzbekistan as a key regional player, citing its population, economic development, and tourism potential. Rubio said the country's reported annual economic growth of nearly 8 percent offered significant opportunities for further cooperation.
He also called for greater US engagement with Central Asia, saying the region had not received the attention it deserved from American policymakers over the past two decades.
The visit was intended to establish a foundation for longer-term cooperation, Rubio said, rather than simply produce a series of immediate commercial agreements.
Critical Minerals And Energy Security
Rubio also highlighted the importance of diversifying global supply chains, particularly for critical minerals used in advanced technologies and industries.
“It's just not smart for the whole world to depend on one place for 100 percent of anything,” he said, arguing that excessive dependence on a single supplier left countries vulnerable to political tensions and disruptions.
Countries with critical minerals and the ability to process them, he said, had an economic interest in developing those resources responsibly. Washington was interested in partnerships that could benefit local economies while diversifying supplies for American and global industries.
On energy, Rubio defended the administration's use of sanctions waivers affecting Russian oil supplies, rejecting the suggestion that the measures meant Washington had changed its position on purchases of Russian energy.
He said decisions had to take into account global prices, energy availability, and the economic circumstances of individual countries, including their ability to find alternative suppliers.
“It's not solely dominated by” the war in Ukraine, Rubio said of US foreign policy, adding that bilateral relationships and broader economic considerations also mattered.
He said Washington was close to a trade deal with India, another factor in the administration's calculations as it sought to balance energy policy and geopolitical priorities.
Rubio Backs Jackson-Vanik Repeal
Rubio also voiced support for repealing the Jackson-Vanik amendment, a Cold War-era US trade restriction that remains a longstanding issue in relations with some former Soviet republics.
Asked by RFE/RL why it had not been repealed, Rubio said the decision rested with Congress, although the administration supported removing the restrictions. “We are in favor of repealing it,” he said, adding that the administration had asked lawmakers to act.
Rubio said he had expressed support for repeal during his Senate confirmation hearings and noted that some members of Congress also favored the move. “Congress just hasn't gotten around to it, but we hope that they will,” he said.
Adopted in 1974, the amendment linked normal trade relations with certain nonmarket economies to emigration rights and other conditions. Originally aimed at Soviet restrictions on Jewish emigration, it has continued to affect US trade policy toward countries that emerged from the Soviet Union.
Repeal would remove a longstanding obstacle to closer economic relations and complement Washington's efforts to expand commercial ties with Central Asia.
Rubio's schedule in Samarkand included meetings with the five Central Asian foreign ministers, talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, and engagements with American business representatives.
He also toured Registan Square, the historic Silk Road landmark that symbolizes Samarkand's centuries-old role as a crossroads of trade.
The visit preceded Rubio's planned trip to India, where US officials said negotiations on a bilateral trade deal were nearing completion.

Macron opens Gulf tour amid violent protests in France

Breadcrumb
Macron opens tour of Gulf states amid violent protests in France
French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday began a Gulf tour aimed at securing oil and diesel supplies in an effort to bring down prices, after a weekend of violent protests sparked by soaring living costs.
Macron, just hours after slamming France's "unbridled" violence in an address late on Sunday, arrived in OPEC member Kuwait where he was welcomed by the emir, Sheikh Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah.
He will also visit the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Qatar by Wednesday on a trip aimed at strengthening "economic and defence partnerships" in the Gulf, which has been thrown into turmoil by the US-Iran war since February.
Macron acknowledged security and intelligence failures but refused his interior minister's resignation after more than 2,500 people were arrested in some of France's worst violence in years, with town halls and shops looted and set on fire.
Before flying to Kuwait, he said the visit was needed to "secure our supplies", pointing out that the demonstrators had expressed "concern" about fuel prices.
Macron's tour "may give an impression of normality... but may also appear out of touch and suggest a kind of power vacuum", said constitutional expert Benjamin Morel.
'Alternative' energy routes
During his trip, "the goal is to secure a certain number of commitments" on diesel and oil volumes, the French presidency said.
Macron is accompanied by senior executives from France's two biggest energy groups, TotalEnergies and Engie.
The G7 countries, chaired this year by France, agreed in early October to draw up to 100 million barrels of oil from their strategic reserves to ease pressure.
Crude oil prices have ballooned during the eight-month war, as Iran blockades the Strait of Hormuz -- the main exit route for the Gulf's energy exports.
Yemen's Houthis have compounded the pressure by firing on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea, striking the kingdom's oil sites and carrying out deadly attacks on Riyadh's international airport.
Francis Perrin, an energy expert at the French Institute for International and Strategic Relations, said he did not expect Macron's visit to have an impact on fuel prices.
"The Arab countries of the Gulf are very eager to supply the world, and the French market, but it is difficult for them to make firm commitments until the region has been stabilised," he said.
Macron will hold talks with Gulf leaders including the UAE's president and Qatar's emir on ways to "secure" maritime shipments and find "alternative and bypass routes" for energy exports, the presidency said.
France and Britain have assembled an international mission to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, mainly through demining operations, once the United States and Iran reach agreement on the waterway.
However, the two sides remain at an impasse, eight months since the start of hostilities.
The French president will also hold talks on defence cooperation, after the Gulf countries were targeted by thousands of Iranian missiles and drones.
France deployed its aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle in the spring, along with Rafale fighter jets, a frigate and air defence assets.
Macron also sent French soldiers to protect Yanbu, an oil terminal on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast that has become a vital conduit for exports.

As of the evening of the 18th of October, 39 injured individuals remained in the hospital, 19 of whom are in critical condition. Firefighters continue to work at the scene to ensure the fire does not reignite. A large quantity of ammunition, grenade launchers, grenades, and small arms were being used at the training ground. 
The fire first broke out approximately one kilometer from the training site and spread rapidly toward the range.
 An investigation is currently underway to determine the cause of the blaze. Rutland explained that intensive activity was taking place throughout the training area, and unusually strong winds caused the flames to spread rapidly, driving them toward the administrative zone of the facility.
Carney stated that the army and fire brigades battled the flames throughout the night under exceptionally difficult conditions. Those affected were in the assault training zone, and the group included reservists.
 On the morning of the 18th of October, the Canadian Army reported that an investigation is ongoing; however, there is no indication that the fire was caused by terrorist activity. At a press conference, Rutland stated that the military does not believe the incident is linked to nearby oil or gas infrastructure, nor does it suspect outside interference. Wainwright Base is located approximately 210 kilometers east of Edmonton, the capital of the province of Alberta, and serves as one of the primary sites where the Canadian Army conducts live-fire exercises. It hosts soldiers from both Canada and allied nations. On a daily basis, the base accommodates around 690 soldiers and 300 civilian personnel.

Kazakh President сalls for expansion of Village Rescuers initiative across Kazakhstan

A central role in training the next generation of rescuers belongs to the Malik Gabdullin Academy of Civil Protection, Kazakhstan's only higher education institution dedicated to preparing civil protection personnel.
The academy is expected to keep pace with technological advances, adopt international best practices and draw lessons from real-world rescue operations. At the same time, it must preserve the continuity of generations and strengthen the traditions of Kazakhstan's emergency response services.

MOSCOW, October 19. /TASS/. Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin has submitted the nominations of five new government members to the State Duma for approval, the Cabinet’s press service reported.
TASS has compiled the key details on the proposed reshuffles.
Putin-Mishustin meeting
- Russian President Vladimir Putin held a working meeting with Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin this morning, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.
- He clarified that, in addition to discussing pressing issues related to the country’s socioeconomic development, the prime minister presented his proposals to the president on a number of reshuffles in the government.
- These proposals received Putin’s support, Peskov added.
Submission of nominees to State Duma for approval
- Mishustin submitted the nominations of five new cabinet members to the State Duma for approval, the government press service reported later.
- State Duma Chairman Vyacheslav Volodin informed lawmakers about the submission of nominations for cabinet positions, the parliament’s website said.
- The State Duma is expected to review them within a week.
- Volodin scheduled an extraordinary meeting of the State Duma Council for October 19 to determine the procedure for approving the new cabinet members, the State Duma press service reported.
Proposed reshuffles
- Mishustin noted that a new position is being created within the government: Deputy Prime Minister - Finance Minister.
- Finance Minister Anton Siluanov has been nominated for this position.
- First Deputy Finance Minister Irina Okladnikova has been nominated for the position of Deputy Prime Minister - Head of the Government Secretariat.
- Transport Minister Andrey Nikitin has been nominated for the position of deputy prime minister, responsible, among other things, for transport development.
- Russia’s Federal Air Transport Agency (Rosaviatsiya) Director Dmitry Yadrov has been nominated for the position of transport minister.
- Primorsky Region Governor Oleg Kozhemyako has been nominated for Deputy Prime Minister - Presidential Plenipotentiary Envoy to the Far Eastern Federal District.
- Yury Trutnev has held this government post since 2013.
- He turned 70 in March.
Nominations for state awards
- Trutnev’s achievements as Deputy Prime Minister - Presidential Plenipotentiary Envoy to the Far Eastern Federal District have been recognized by the president, and he will be nominated for a high state award, the government press service noted.
- According to him, now former Deputy Prime Minister Dmitry Grigorenko will also be nominated for a high state award for his service in that position.
Work of deputy prime ministers
- All deputy prime ministers will continue in their posts until the relevant presidential decrees are issued, Peskov noted.
- Vera Shcherbina will serve as acting governor of the Primorsky Region if Kozhemyako leaves for Moscow, the regional government reported.
